newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina may hike fuel prices to fund new roads.
newsitem.headline: Argentina may hike fuel prices to fund new roads.

text.p: The Argentine government is studying a price hike of $0.10 per liter for gasoline and diesel to fuel a major road-building program, Undersecretary for Tax Policy Guillermo Rodriguez Use said Wednesday.

President Carlos Menem has announced plans to build 10,000 km of national highways to link up the country's major cities. Menem said the investment needed would be $10 billion and 30,000 jobs could be created.

Rodriguez Use, commenting on newspaper reports that the road project would be financed by a new fuel tax, told reporters: "Yes, we are studying that and it would be a 10 cent hike on petrol and 10 cents on diesel."

Menem, keen to present job-creating plans ahead of key mid-term elections for Congress in October, said Tuesday the bidding process for the road project would be under way before the end of the year and building would start by June 1998.
Last year Economy Minister Roque Fernandez introduced tax hikes of 10-15 percent on gasoline and 40 percent on diesel, which came into effect in Octobe, to narrow a budget deficit.
